title: 🎸🎨Interview with A. Savage of the Parquet Courts Psychology of Visual Art and Music

sentences.en: That boy needs therapy.
sentences.zh: 那孩子需要心理治疗。

sentences.en: Lie down on the couch.
sentences.zh: 躺到沙发上去。

sentences.en: Hi, this is Joel Blackstock with the Taproot Therapy Collective PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是 Joel Blackstock，这是“Taproot 治疗集体”播客。

sentences.en: And this week I sat down with A.
sentences.zh: 本周我采访了 A.

sentences.en: Savage, a musician and visual artiSt.
sentences.zh: Savage，一位音乐家兼视觉艺术家。

sentences.en: His band, The Parquet Courts, is one of my favorites.
sentences.zh: 他的乐队 Parquet Courts 是我的心头好之一。

sentences.en: They have a thoughtful kind of art rock insight into our culture that's sometimes acerbic, sometimes humorous.
sentences.zh: 他们对我们文化有着一种深思熟虑的艺术摇滚洞察，有时尖刻，有时幽默。

sentences.en: Always very fun to listen to.
sentences.zh: 听起来总是非常有趣。

sentences.en: And he has very interesting visual art that kind of suggests movement, emotion, fresh, interesting, and graphic.
sentences.zh: 他还有非常有趣的视觉艺术作品，给人一种动感、情感丰富、新颖、有趣且具有图形感的感觉。

sentences.en: We'll link to both of his websites for his projects in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 我们会在节目介绍中附上他两个项目的网站链接。

sentences.en: But I hope you guys enjoy the interview, The Psychology of Music with A.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期访谈，《音乐心理学与 A.》

sentences.en: Savage.
sentences.zh: Savage。

sentences.en: And we're enormously grateful that he sat down to talk with us.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感谢他能坐下来与我们交谈。

sentences.en: So without further ado, I'll go ahead and roll that interview.
sentences.zh: 那么，废话不多说，让我们直接进入访谈。

sentences.en: One of the reasons that we're having you on is to talk about kind of the relationship to trauma and creativity and just the creative process of the unconscious.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请你来的原因之一，是想聊聊创伤与创造力之间的关系，以及潜意识的创作过程。

sentences.en: But also, you know, just what people see into the mind of a creative that's successful.
sentences.zh: 同时也想让大家了解一下成功创作者的内心世界。

sentences.en: Because we work with a lot of younger people.
sentences.zh: 因为我们接触很多年轻人。

sentences.en: A lot of people that like your music.
sentences.zh: 很多人都喜欢你的音乐。

sentences.en: A lot of people that just like creativity in general.
sentences.zh: 很多人单纯就是热爱创造力。

sentences.en: And I think like being able to see what somebody's process is is so empowering.
sentences.zh: 我认为能够看到一个人的创作过程是非常赋能的。

sentences.en: Especially right now when everything is so atomized.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在现在这个一切都如此原子化的时代。

sentences.en: We started this like, we called it a social encounter group recently just because every clinician was hearing from everybody who was like, you know, 20 to 30.
sentences.zh: 我们最近发起了这个活动，称之为“社交邂逅小组”，因为每个临床医生都在听 20 到 30 岁的人说：

sentences.en: Like, I don't want to go to church and I don't want to go to bars and I don't know anywhere else to meet people.
sentences.zh: “我不想去教堂，也不想去酒吧，我不知道还能去哪里结识新朋友。”

sentences.en: And all my friends are on Discord and it's either not healthy or it's, you know, limited.
sentences.zh: “我所有的朋友都在 Discord 上，要么不健康，要么（社交圈）很有限。”

sentences.en: And how do I do that?
sentences.zh: “我该怎么办？”

sentences.en: And, you know, none of us had an answer.
sentences.zh: 我们谁也给不出答案。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're like, okay, we're going to do this mixer.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想，好吧，我们来办这个联谊会。

sentences.en: And then y'all are encouraged afterwards to go out to eat and, you know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 活动结束后，鼓励大家去聚餐，或者做点别的什么。

sentences.en: It's not group therapy.
sentences.zh: 这不是团体治疗。

sentences.en: It's really just an opportunity to encounter, you know, the creative and spiritual and personal aspect of life that we never get a chance to anymore, you know?
sentences.zh: 这真的只是一个机会，去接触生活中那些我们再也没有机会触及的创造性、精神性和个人层面，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that is something that is kind of disappearing or rather becoming more online is is people meeting and like, well, it's I mean,
sentences.zh: 是啊，那种人与人面对面交流的方式确实在消失，或者说变得越来越线上化了，嗯，我的意思是，

sentences.en: it's a way that's just kind of affected culture, really.
sentences.zh: 这确实以某种方式影响了文化。

sentences.en: Whereas one point, like people would have met, you know, and you mentioned you mentioned church.
sentences.zh: 以前人们会见面，你提到了教堂。

sentences.en: But, you know, like at a show or like at some sort of place where like minded people go for me, it was like I met a lot of my friends like in the DIY scene around the US.
sentences.zh: 但比如在演出中，或者在志同道合的人聚集的地方，对我来说，我很多朋友都是在美国各地的 DIY 圈子里认识的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's it's it's it's important to keep that it's important to keep the quality of that sort of interaction, because ultimately that is, I think,
sentences.zh: 但保持那种互动质量非常重要，因为归根结底，我认为，

sentences.en: something that cultivates creativity and just genuine connection in a way that online interaction, though, you know.
sentences.zh: 这才是培养创造力和建立真正联系的方式，而线上互动虽然，你知道，

sentences.en: You know, it does have its pros just can't, you know,
sentences.zh: 它确实有优点，但就是无法，你知道，

sentences.en: and that's something I've noticed is that things just kind of are part of culture and especially part of young people's culture is increasingly about being online,
sentences.zh: 我注意到的一点是，现在很多事物，尤其是年轻人的文化，越来越倾向于线上，

sentences.en: which just doesn't it doesn't provide the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能提供同样的东西。

sentences.en: Well, and it's interesting because I think that like you see kind of the boomers come up and a lot of their parents are, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这很有趣，因为我觉得你可以看到婴儿潮一代成长起来，他们的父母很多，你知道，

sentences.en: coming from a harder economic situation than they had.
sentences.zh: 经历的经济状况比他们自己要艰难。

sentences.en: And they their parents kind of over provide for the boomers, you know, material support, but they don't give them a ton of emotional support.
sentences.zh: 父母对婴儿潮一代在物质上过度供给，但在情感支持上却给得不多。

sentences.en: And, of course, this is just broad strokes, not everyone's experiences like this.
sentences.zh: 当然，这只是笼统的说法，并非每个人的经历都如此。

sentences.en: And so the boomers kids, the millennials are more like they're really into authenticity and this kind of personal journey.
sentences.zh: 所以婴儿潮一代的孩子，也就是千禧一代，他们更看重真实性和这种个人旅程。

sentences.en: And it gets silly at a certain point where you're like, you know, well,
sentences.zh: 但有时候这会变得很荒谬，比如，你知道，

sentences.en: this brewery is going to have the Edison Classic light bulb hung up on the cast iron pipe to be raw and authentic.
sentences.zh: 这家啤酒厂非要在铸铁管上挂个爱迪生复古灯泡，好显得原始又真实。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're going to turn everything into every part of life into this high type of art.
sentences.zh: 我们要把生活的每一个部分都变成这种高雅艺术。

sentences.en: And, you know, I mean, there's it's good, but there, you know, it gets silly as that kind of takes over.
sentences.zh: 这当然是好事，但当这种风气占据主导时，就显得很傻了。

sentences.en: And then the millennials kids, it's like they're they grow up in with this therapy language almost where they, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后是千禧一代的孩子，他们成长过程中几乎满口治疗术语，你知道，

sentences.en: it's not that it's bad to have that level of personal development and search for, you know, your authentic self online.
sentences.zh: 拥有那种个人成长水平和在线上寻找真实自我的过程本身并不坏。

sentences.en: But, you know, you're like, all right, guys, it's time to take the ACT and they're like, no,
sentences.zh: 但有时候你会想，好吧，各位，该去采取行动了，他们却说，不，

sentences.en: I need I need my 17th adjective in front of my sexuality or my particular brand of communism.
sentences.zh: 我需要在我的性取向或我特定的共产主义流派前面加上第 17 个形容词。

sentences.en: And it's like, no, that's that's fine.
sentences.zh: 这当然没问题。

sentences.en: You know, but also you need to touch grass like, you know, you've got 13 people in Kazakhstan that share your your politics, you know, and realize it's happening.
sentences.zh: 但你也得“脚踏实地”啊，你在哈萨克斯坦有 13 个人和你政见相同，你要意识到现实生活正在发生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And it is nice that they're able to find those people and have that, you know, awareness of who they are earlier in life.
sentences.zh: 他们能找到志同道合的人，并在人生早期就拥有这种自我认知，这确实很好。

sentences.en: But also there's just so few skills that even like my generation took for granted, you know,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他们缺乏很多连我们这一代人都视为理所当然的技能，你知道，

sentences.en: that was so you were talking about before we started recording the way that the kind of therapy that we do.
sentences.zh: 在我们开始录音之前，你谈到了我们所做的这种治疗方式。

sentences.en: Are you familiar kind of do you have any kind of psychology background or have you been to therapy?
sentences.zh: 你熟悉吗？你有什么心理学背景吗？或者你做过心理治疗吗？

sentences.en: Are you comfortable saying that if you have or I have?
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意说的话，或者我做过。

sentences.en: But I, you know, the first time I ever went to therapy, I was I was 29.
sentences.zh: 但我第一次去心理治疗时，我已经 29 岁了。

sentences.en: I was almost, you know, in my 30s.
sentences.zh: 快 30 岁了。

sentences.en: So, you know, I went as an adult and it was not part of my culture growing up.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在成年后才去的，这在我成长过程中并不是一种文化。

sentences.en: And it was I mean, for most of my life, it was something that I thought I would never need.
sentences.zh: 在我生命的大部分时间里，我以为我永远都不需要它。

sentences.en: So, you know, I came late to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我接触得比较晚。

sentences.en: So, no, I didn't grow up with the language of therapy like I mean, I know some people, especially people that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，我并不是在治疗语言中长大的，我的意思是，我认识一些人，尤其是那些，你知道，

sentences.en: kind of grew up here in New York where I live and have lived for 13 years.
sentences.zh: 在纽约这种地方长大的人，我住在这里已经 13 年了。

sentences.en: There's I know people who were born into therapy, basically, but that was not that was not my experience at all.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些基本上是“在治疗中出生”的人，但这完全不是我的经历。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is interesting.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这很有趣。

sentences.en: And New York is like one of the only places where psychoanalysis, psychoanalysis, like pure psychoanalysis is still kicking.
sentences.zh: 纽约是少数几个精神分析——纯粹的精神分析——依然活跃的地方之一。

sentences.en: You know, it's just kind of normal for people here to talk about their analysts like it's a what do you hear or something?
sentences.zh: 在这里，人们谈论他们的分析师就像谈论……你懂的，很正常。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And you don't I mean, pure psychoanalysis really anywhere else is just gone, but it is still kind of around there.
sentences.zh: 在其他地方，纯粹的精神分析几乎消失了，但在那里依然存在。

sentences.en: Maybe because Anna Freud settles there and it kind of has a established, you know, what do you call pure psychoanalysis?
sentences.zh: 也许是因为安娜·弗洛伊德在那里定居，建立了一种，你所谓的纯粹精神分析？

sentences.en: Is that I mean, I mean, because even like I don't really know how to classify the therapy that I've had.
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？因为我甚至不知道该如何归类我所接受的治疗。

sentences.en: But is that just like talk therapy, laying down in the chaise lounge while someone takes notes?
sentences.zh: 那只是谈话疗法吗？躺在躺椅上，有人在旁边做笔记？

sentences.en: Pretty much.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's interesting you mentioned that.
sentences.zh: 你提到这一点很有意思。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a big conversation, but the field starts with, you know, Freud says there's an unconscious and what it is, is it's full of sex and violence.
sentences.zh: 这是一个宏大的话题，但这个领域始于弗洛伊德，他说存在潜意识，里面充满了性和暴力。

sentences.en: And then he, you know, Freud has this he's raised by his mom that you're brilliant, you're going to be great.
sentences.zh: 然后他，你知道，弗洛伊德的母亲把他养大，告诉他你是天才，你会很伟大。

sentences.en: And he says, but his dad is extremely passive.
sentences.zh: 但他父亲却极其被动。

sentences.en: His dad would get like beaten up in the street by anti-Semites.
sentences.zh: 他父亲会在街上被反犹分子殴打。

sentences.en: And Freud would have these like the fantasies that his dad was like Hannibal of Carthage and write about it.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德会幻想他父亲是迦太基的汉尼拔，并写下这些幻想。

sentences.en: Like he needed to be dominant, but he also couldn't assert himself in conflict.
sentences.zh: 他需要变得强势，但在冲突中却无法坚持自我。

sentences.en: There's this weird kind of thing where Freud put everybody up on this pedestal and was like, you're going to be the bulwark that carries on my teaching.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的现象，弗洛伊德把每个人都捧上神坛，说“你将成为传承我教义的堡垒”。

sentences.en: And then they become a version of him that isn't good when they have their own ideas.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们有了自己的想法时，他们就变成了他不喜欢的样子。

sentences.en: And then he knocks them off and finds another one.
sentences.zh: 于是他把他们踢开，再找下一个。

sentences.en: And so Jung and Adler and Autorank and everyone that happens.
sentences.zh: 荣格、阿德勒、奥托·兰克，每个人都经历了这些。

sentences.en: Jung, which I agree with a lot more, says, you know, the unconscious is not just sex and violence.
sentences.zh: 荣格——我更认同他——说，潜意识不仅仅是性和暴力。

sentences.en: Maybe that's what's in your shadow.
sentences.zh: 也许那是你阴影里的东西。

sentences.en: But there's these evolutionary forces that are kind of older than us that are in the unconscious and the ego is sort of reacting to them.
sentences.zh: 但潜意识里还有一些比我们更古老的进化力量，自我只是在对它们做出反应。

sentences.en: But to really heal and integrate, you have to crack the ego open and start to feel some of this stuff, which gets taken a lot of directions.
sentences.zh: 但要真正治愈和整合，你必须打破自我，开始感受这些东西，这在后来被引向了许多方向。

sentences.en: And so the short history of the profession, just real quick, is, you know, Adler and Freud and, you know, Adler's more about relationships, but they're dealing with an unconscious.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个职业的简史，简单来说，就是阿德勒和弗洛伊德，阿德勒更关注人际关系，但他们都在处理潜意识。

sentences.en: Like, what is it that's bigger than us that we're not, even though I'm thinking about this one thing, I'm responding to a lot of forces beneath the surface.
sentences.zh: 比如，有什么比我们更宏大的东西？即使我在思考这一件事，我其实是在响应表面之下的许多力量。

sentences.en: And when you have Reagan and Thatcher come in in the 80s and health care is incredibly corporatized and education is incredibly corporatized academics, then they say, OK,
sentences.zh: 当 80 年代里根和撒切尔上台，医疗保健和教育被极度企业化、学术化时，他们说，好吧，

sentences.en: none of that's real.
sentences.zh: 那些都不是真的。

sentences.en: And that's all coming.
sentences.zh: 那都是胡扯。

sentences.en: Like, none of that is effective.
sentences.zh: 那根本没用。

sentences.en: This is woo woo.
sentences.zh: 这是伪科学。

sentences.en: We're not paying for energy patterns.
sentences.zh: 我们不为能量模式买单。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: At the same time, Beck is coming out with cognitive behavioral therapy, which is a reaction to psychoanalysis.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，贝克提出了认知行为疗法（CBT），这是对精神分析的一种反动。

sentences.en: And he's like, what's the point of talking about why you smoke cigarettes?
sentences.zh: 他说，讨论你为什么抽烟有什么意义？

sentences.en: What your mom did to make you smoke cigarettes on the couch for 30 years while you smoke cigarettes?
sentences.zh: 讨论你妈做了什么让你在沙发上抽了 30 年烟有什么意义？

sentences.en: The only thing that's real is behavior.
sentences.zh: 唯一真实的就是行为。

sentences.en: So we're just going to measure behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只测量行为。

sentences.en: Did the behavior change?
sentences.zh: 行为改变了吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, there's some therapists that say they do cognitive behavioral therapy, but you get to know them and they are doing more than that.
sentences.zh: 有些治疗师声称他们做的是认知行为疗法，但你深入了解后会发现他们做的远不止这些。

sentences.en: But, I mean, pure CBT is, you know, so psychoanalysis, you're saying what's the difference in that and like 40 and psychodynamic, whatever, you know,
sentences.zh: 但纯粹的 CBT，你知道，所以精神分析，你问它和心理动力学有什么区别，你知道，

sentences.en: psychoanalysis is just analysis.
sentences.zh: 精神分析就是分析。

sentences.en: There's no experience.
sentences.zh: 没有体验。

sentences.en: The therapist is very minimal.
sentences.zh: 治疗师的角色非常微小。

sentences.en: You are just analyzing what somebody is doing.
sentences.zh: 你只是在分析某人在做什么。

sentences.en: You know, psychodynamic, Freudian therapy, you're maybe holding the role of the parent or, you know, saying, well, your relationship with me,
sentences.zh: 心理动力学，弗洛伊德式的治疗，你可能扮演了父母的角色，或者说，嗯，你和我之间的关系，

sentences.en: that's how maybe your relationship with other people are.
sentences.zh: 可能就是你和其他人关系的缩影。

sentences.en: And this pattern pops up in here or something.
sentences.zh: 这种模式在这里显现出来了，之类的。

sentences.en: So when behavioral cognitive therapy comes out, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以当认知行为疗法出现时，你知道，

sentences.en: I don't like it because we deal with trauma patients and it tends to re-traumatize them because what you're doing with CBT is just moving anxiety around.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢它，因为我们处理创伤患者，它往往会造成二次创伤，因为 CBT 所做的只是转移焦虑。

sentences.en: You're saying like, okay, well, you drink six beers a day.
sentences.zh: 它会说，好吧，你每天喝六瓶啤酒。

sentences.en: Why don't you drink three beers a day and play three games of Monopoly?
sentences.zh: 为什么不每天喝三瓶，然后玩三局大富翁呢？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Now play six games of Monopoly, drink no beers, you're cured because the number went down.
sentences.zh: 现在玩六局大富翁，不喝啤酒，你治愈了，因为数字下降了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The thing behind the behavior.
sentences.zh: 行为背后的东西呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It's like, where is that in your body?
sentences.zh: 就像是，它在你的身体里哪里？

sentences.en: How old is that?
sentences.zh: 它有多久了？

sentences.en: You know, we don't care how much beer you're drinking.
sentences.zh: 我们不在乎你喝多少啤酒。

sentences.en: What do you feel when you're not drinking beer?
sentences.zh: 你不喝啤酒时感觉如何？

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你懂吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And, and so that trauma informed stuff that is using emotion is using the support of cool brain and the body is coming back because, I mean, really it's coming back because,
sentences.zh: 所以那种利用情感、利用大脑和身体支持的创伤知情疗法正在回归，因为，我的意思是，它回归是因为，

sentences.en: you know, insurance is realizing that it costs more money to put a bandaid on something forever, you know, than to treat it.
sentences.zh: 保险公司意识到，给伤口贴一辈子创可贴的成本，比治疗它要高得多。
